params.body:
**Merge order: merge the other open pull requests first, then this one.** Pull requests that regenerate these files are still open (the vehicle sheet one; the Car-Pass dialog one merged as #323 and this branch is rebased on it). This one deletes those files, so whoever merges second gets a delete/modify conflict. Merge them, then this.

## What

`docs/bedrijfsregels.html` and the coverage table leave git. They are generated from `docs/bedrijfsregels/*.md` and the `@rule` tags in the tests, so every pull request that adds or changes a rule regenerates them, and two such pull requests always collide. That happened four times on 14 September, and each collision costs a whole new pull request because the gateway cannot update an existing branch.

This is the same move the repository made on 12 September for `public/build`, the vendor copies in `public/js` and the purged theme CSS: the source stays in git, the output is made on request, and CI proves the making still works.

## One thing was not as it looked

`docs/bedrijfsregels/92-testdekking.md` is not a generated file. `--write` only replaced a block between two markers; the other thirty lines are hand-written analysis (what is tested and what is not, the test debt ranked by risk). Taking the whole file out of git would have deleted that analysis, and `--write` would have stopped working, because it reads the file it edits.

So the generated half was split off: `bin/rules-coverage --write` now writes a whole chapter of its own, `docs/bedrijfsregels/92-testdekking-tabel.md`, which is gitignored. `92-testdekking.md` keeps its history and its prose and points at the generated chapter. `--write` also takes `--out=` now, so it can be run without touching the working tree.

## The guard

`tests/Feature/RulesDocsBuildTest` runs both generators into a throwaway path and fails if either errors or writes nothing. It goes next to `RulesCoverageTest` rather than into the `assets` CI job because the generators are PHP and that job has no PHP toolchain, and because the existing guard for this document is already a test that shells out to `bin/rules-coverage`: a test also catches the break locally, before CI. It never compares the output against a committed file, which would reintroduce exactly what this removes.

## References updated

- `CLAUDE.md`, Business rules: the regenerate line now names both outputs, plus a line saying they are not committed and why.
- `README.md`: two places, the overview line and the tooling line.
- `docs/bedrijfsregels/00-inleiding.md`: the page is made on request.
- `bin/rules-coverage`: header comment, the snapshot path, `--out=`, and the write block.

`CUTOVER.md` and the workflows have no reference to either path. `docs/` is not served by the application.

No open point in `91-o-open-punten.md` covers this, so none was marked done and none was added.

## Verified

- `php artisan test --filter='RulesCoverage|RulesDocsBuild'`: 3 tests green.
- Full suite: 1 failed, 652 warnings, 61 passed (2938 assertions). The single failure is `BuildStampTest`, the known worktree artifact (`.git` is a file in a worktree); the warnings are the missing `.env` in the worktree, on every test.
- Both generators run twice in a row and give the same 719 rules, with the generated chapter in their own input.
params.title: The rules page and the coverage table leave git
